intro: This branch explores three-dimensional solids: what their slices look like, how to find their surface areas and volumes, and why the formulas work. A few skills include short arguments where the learner puts steps in order or picks what they prove.

V.14.01.what: A cross-section is the flat shape you see when you slice straight through a solid, like cutting a loaf of bread.

levels.a: Names the shape of a slice through a box or other prism.
levels.b: Names the shape of a slice through a pyramid.
levels.c: Finds the area of a slice through a cylinder or cone, such as a cut through a cone's tip.
levels.d: Names the slice through a cube cut at an unusual angle, such as a triangle or hexagon.

V.14.02.what: Spinning a flat shape around a line sweeps out a solid, like a potter's wheel shaping clay.

levels.a: Finds the radius and height of the cylinder made by spinning a rectangle.
levels.b: Finds the radius and height of the cone made by spinning a right triangle.
levels.c: Finds the radius of the sphere made by spinning a half circle.
levels.d: Finds the volume of the solid made, taking care which side becomes the radius.

V.14.03.what: Cavalieri's principle: if two solids have equal-area slices at every height and the same height, they have equal volume, like a straight or slanted stack of coins.

levels.a: Uses equal slices to find the volume of a slanted solid from an upright one.
levels.b: Finds the volume or upright height of a slanted box.
levels.c: Finds the volume of a slanted cylinder, working out its upright height first.
levels.d: Puts in order the steps that find a sphere's volume by comparing it with a cylinder minus a cone.

V.14.04.what: Finding the total outside area of pyramids and cones by adding the area of the base and the slanted sides.

levels.a: Finds the slant height, measured along the sloping side, using Pythagoras.
levels.b: Finds the area of the sloping sides only (the lateral area).
levels.c: Adds the base to find the total surface area.
levels.d: Works from a flat net (the shape unfolded) to find the size of a cone.

V.14.05.what: Finding the outside area of a sphere, which is exactly 4 times the area of a circle with the same radius.

levels.a: Finds a sphere's surface area from its radius.
levels.b: Finds the area of a solid half-sphere, including its flat face.
levels.c: Works backwards from the area to find the radius.
levels.d: Explores Archimedes' discovery: a sphere fills two thirds of the cylinder that just fits around it.

V.14.06.what: A pyramid or cone holds exactly one third of the prism or cylinder with the same base and height.

levels.a: Picks what a short argument proves: by splitting a cube into 6 pyramids, a pyramid is one third of its prism.
levels.b: Finds the volume of a pyramid or cone.
levels.c: Works backwards from the volume to find a missing height or radius.
levels.d: Finds the volume of a frustum, a cone or pyramid with its top sliced off.
levels.e: Finds how full a cone-shaped glass is, knowing volume grows with the cube of the height.
levels.f: Finds the volume of a pyramid hidden inside a cube by cutting away the corners.

V.14.07.what: Finding the volume and surface area of objects built from several simple solids.

levels.a: Adds the volumes of the parts.
levels.b: Subtracts the volume of a hole that has been cut out.
levels.c: Finds the outside area of a combined solid, leaving out the hidden faces.
levels.d: Applies this to real objects, such as a capsule-shaped pill.
levels.e: Works out how many smaller solids can be cast from a melted-down larger one.
levels.f: Counts every face, including inside tunnels, to find the surface area of a complicated solid.

V.14.08.what: Using volume and area in real design problems, such as density and making packages efficient.

levels.a: Finds density, how heavy something is for its size, as mass divided by volume.
levels.b: Finds population density, people per square kilometer.
levels.c: Picks the box shape that holds a set amount using the least material.
levels.d: Works out how many items fit in a package, rounding down for partial items.
